'''Peter Michael Harman''' (11 December 1943 – 14 August 2014) was a British historian who was Professor of the History of Science at the [[Lancaster University|University of Lancaster]].

== Career ==
Harman was born in [[Leeds]], Yorkshire, the son of Herbert and Gertrude (nee Harris) Heimann. He studied at [[Oriel College]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] and later at the [[University of Leeds]]. He was [[Lecturer|Assistant Lecturer]] at the [[University of Glasgow]] (1969–70) and at the [[University of Cambridge]] (1970–74) where he was a Fellow of [[Clare Hall, Cambridge|Clare Hall]] (1971–74), before being appointed Lecturer at the [[University of Lancaster]] in 1974. He was appointed [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] in 1993 and professor in 1999 until his retirement in 2007.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Peter Harman – Research Portal {{!}} Lancaster University |url=http://www.research.lancs.ac.uk/portal/en/people/peter-harman(2555ba94-90eb-4ba4-a0d7-06d9281b7c8e).html |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=www.research.lancs.ac.uk}}</ref>

Harman was a [[Visiting scholar]] at [[Harvard University]] (1988–89 and 1990–91). As Zeeman Professor of the History of Physics at the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1995, his lectures were on the topic of ''The Natural Philosophy of James Clerk Maxwell'' and were later published.<ref name=":0" />

[[File:Lancaster University 31 Alexandra Square 6002.JPG|thumbnail| Alexandra Square, [[Lancaster University]] ]]
Harman's research was focussed chiefly on the history of natural philosophy and physics in the 18th and 19th centuries, covering the period after [[Isaac Newton]], with his most important work being his research on the physicist [[James Clerk Maxwell]], which was supported by the [[Royal Society]], the [[Leverhulme Trust]] (1986–87), the [[National Science Foundation]] (1988–89 and 1990–91), and the [[Arts and Humanities Research Board]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/alumni/in-memoriam/ |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=University of Lancaster |language=en}}</ref>
